_note: Districts made of the packs' own demo scenes, whole, as their artists assembled them (Phase 25: the owner, 2026-09-28, 'redo one of the corner, smaller districts with the exact assets from the bought packs ... we should barely see differences'). Each takes a pack's demo scene (`scene`, its Unity path), turns it `yaw` about the scene point `origin` and moves that point to `at` (map-local metres), and keeps the parts whose middle lands in one of `keep` (x >= x0 and z >= z0: the map's corner, its edges' blocks either side and what lies past the map's edge, the backdrop) within `radius` metres of `at`. tools/import-city.ts bakes it (CITY_DISTRICTS=1) into public/models/paid/city/<id>-v<version>.glb (and <id>-v<version>-lo.glb at the kit's lo texture size, for the presets that load the kit's lo files) and writes `measured` back here: its triangles and bounds, never typed. `blocks`: the city's blocks (column and row, 0 to 6) it replaces, built and taken away again so the city's stream draws as before. High City's is a crossroads of deep canyons, walkways along its faces: turned a quarter so its two long arms (70 and 51 m) run inside the map along its east and south edges, and its two short ones point out past the edge. `hole`: the district's ground plan (map-local x, z), where its look holds; with `bottomless` the street's plane is left open over it so its canyons fall away as in the pack's own scene, and without, the street is the canyons' floor, joined to the city's streets at the ends of its arms (the playable one). `look`: its haze (`day` and `night` colours, from `near` to `far` metres; a `near` behind the camera thickens the first metres as the store's haze does, where our haze is linear) and its light (the hour's sun and sky's fill scaled by `sun` and `env`: the store's pictures are soft and hazy, not sunlit) where you stand in it, by eye against High City's store pictures, from Balanced up as the city's haze is, and `shadows`: its buildings shade its own canyons as the pack's lighting does. `look grade`: the colour grade over the game's while you stand in it (render.ts setLook: split tone, contrast, saturation, vignette), the store's cool, flat, grey-green, vignetted look; Balanced and High, which have the grade. `look backs`: its opaque faces drawn from behind too (the film set is faced only toward its canyons, and from the city's streets round it only its frames showed, a building you saw through). `look glow`: its lit windows' and signs' light scaled by the hour, `day` and `night` (the store's daytime pictures have their windows dark). `collision`: how tools/import-city.ts districtSolids makes each district's boxes from its own triangles (the pack scene is faces, never boxes): a grid of `cell` metres, each cell filled over the heights its triangles span there, spans nearer than `merge` joined, one thinner than `thin` made that deep, nothing under `floor` (the street is the floor) nor topping out under `minTop`, and a part whose middle size is under `stick` (a cable, a wire, a pole) left out; written to src/config/districts/<id>.solids.json. `fill`: the collision behind the film set's faces (districtSolids): a cell whose top is a walkway (between walkway[0] and walkway[1] metres) solid down to the street, and every cell of the district's plan within the map (`half`) that the street reachable on foot from the canyons' `seeds` (map-local x, z) does not reach, solid: its buildings, a cell with something drawn in it to the top of what is drawn, and one with nothing (the film set's hollow inside) to the height of the nearest cells that have, `top` only where none is; and a hollow cell joined through hollow cells to the plan's edge (the scene's open ground round its buildings, not a building's inside) to `open` metres, far over anything you reach, and not drawn (a fixed 40 m put an invisible floor over every lower building and empty lot, the owner's "glitch into the corner map area"); what city draws of the hollow cells (covers and caps in the collision file) closes the film set from above and through its windows; and anything whose foot is less than `body` metres over the street or a walkway reaches down to it (a crate's or a car's top alone in a cell, its sides in the cells round it, hovered over the walkway, a ledge a bot walked into), and a cell with walkway on two sides and more is on the walkway, its own height or the walkway's (a lamp post's foot, a gap in the deck; filled to `top`, a lamp post was a pillar 40 m high). `pads`: the jump pads up from the canyons' floor to the walkways, each [x, z, nx, nz]: a spot on the floor (map-local) and the way out of the walkway's front toward it; city.ts walks back from the spot, up to `padReach` metres, to the first box of the collision that stands on the street with a walkway's top, and throws you from its face onto that top (padOnto), so a pad follows the walkway it serves through a re-bake. `escapes`: fire escapes up the walkways' fronts from the canyons' floor, the packs' own (the owner, 2026-09-28: "pretty sure there are versions in the asset packs"), built as the city's are (city.json fireEscape, citykit.json dress escapes `family`, measured off the pieces): each walks back from `spot` against `out` (the front's way out, as a pad's) to the same box a pad finds, hangs on that front's plane with its middle at the spot, and has a landing each whole storey under the walkway and the climb from the last onto it; one that the city's rules turn down (something solid in its way, a pad within fireEscape clear.pad) is left out, and tools/checks/sk-district.ts fails. It lands you `padLand` metres past the front: High City's walkways carry a line of posts 0.95 m high, one every 2 m, 2.5 to 2.75 m behind their fronts (the collision's cross-sections; the rails between them are thinner than `stick`), and the city's own 3 m put you on top of one. `bots`: the district on the bots' graph (city.ts): each of `canyons` a line of points (map-local) down a canyon's middle, its first on the city's street past an arm's end, a node every `step` metres along it, the first joined to that street's crossings either side; and on its walkways a node every `grid` metres of the plan where the collision's top is a walkway's, linked to those round it, kept where the walk reaches from a pad's landing (a line of nodes laid along High City's walkways stopped at their posts, bollards, bins and parked cars); every link one a bot walks both ways, and the pads on the graph one way up, as the centre's are. The flood keeps to `streets` ([x0, x1, z0, z1], map-local): the canyons' floors, a little wider than the walkways' fronts measured off the collision's cross-sections (the vertical canyon open from x 127.5 to 139.5 along its length, the horizontal from z 125.5 to 140.5), so it cannot run out at an arm's end, where the walkways have not begun, and behind the faces into the empty film set.
